subject: geography
title: Rivers & Coasts Adventure: Foundations
welcome_lead: Every river and every coast does the same three jobs: erode, transport, deposit. Let's meet them.
meta_desc: GCSE Geography rivers and coasts basics — erosion, transportation, deposition processes.
final_note: You learned the four types of erosion and four types of transportation.

concepts.def: Force of water hits and breaks rock
Rocks scrape and grind against bedrock
Rocks knock together and become smoother/smaller
Heavy rocks rolled along river/sea bed

walkthroughs.body_html:
Rivers and waves erode in the same four ways:

Hydraulic action: pure force of water compressing air in cracks.
Abrasion: load scrapes the channel/cliff.
Attrition: load rocks knock together, getting smaller and rounder.
Solution: chemical — water dissolves limestone and chalk.

Traction: large boulders rolled along.
Saltation: smaller pebbles bounce.
Suspension: fine sand/silt held in the flow.
Solution (transport): dissolved minerals carried invisibly.

When energy drops, the load is dropped.

Rivers deposit on the inside of meanders, on flood plains, and at the mouth (delta/estuary).

Coasts deposit in sheltered bays (beaches) or where currents weaken (spits, bars).

mcqs.q: Which erosion process involves rocks KNOCKING TOGETHER and becoming smoother?
What transport process carries DISSOLVED minerals invisibly in water?
